questionText:
Consider the following four variable Boolean function in sum-of-product form
$$F(b_3, b_2, b_1, b_0) = \sum(0, 2, 4, 8, 10, 11, 12).$$
where the value of the function is computed by considering $b_3 b_2 b_1 b_0$ as a 4-bit binary number, where $b_3$ denotes the most significant bit and $b_0$ denotes the least significant bit. Note that there are no don't care terms. Which ONE of the following options is the CORRECT minimized Boolean expression for $F$?
explanation:
To find the minimized Boolean expression for $F(b_3, b_2, b_1, b_0) = \sum(0, 2, 4, 8, 10, 11, 12)$, we can group the minterms using a 4-variable K-map:

Minterms in binary form ($b_3 b_2 b_1 b_0$):
• $0 = 0000$
• $2 = 0010$
• $4 = 0100$
• $8 = 1000$
• $10 = 1010$
• $11 = 1011$
• $12 = 1100$

Grouping the minterms:
1. Group of 4 minterms $(0, 2, 8, 10)$: Gives the term $\bar{b}_1 \bar{b}_0$
2. Group of 4 minterms $(0, 4, 8, 12)$: Gives the term $\bar{b}_2 \bar{b}_0$
3. Group of 2 minterms $(10, 11)$: Minterm $11$ ($1011$) needs to be covered. Grouping $10$ ($1010$) and $11$ ($1011$) gives $b_3 \bar{b}_2 b_1$

Combining these prime implicants, we get:
$F = \bar{b}_1 \bar{b}_0 + \bar{b}_2 \bar{b}_0 + b_1 \bar{b}_2 b_3$

Thus, Option A is the correct minimized expression.
